mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the effect reverses during a recession.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with falling housing starts (HOUST) signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST 3-month change < -10%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the relationship inverts during periods of strong productivity growth.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the unemployment rate below 4% for three consecutive months, accompanied by a concurrent rise in average hourly earnings (proxied by PAYEMS growth), signals a tight labor market with upward wage pressure. This increases input costs and reduces profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4% for 3 consecutive months AND PAYEMS 3-month change > 0.5%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or the effect disappears during periods of high inflation.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for four consecutive months signals a broad-based contraction in manufacturing output, reducing corporate sales and earnings, and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -0.5% for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly different from zero in triggered episodes, or the effect is reversed during supply-chain normalization.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-month decline in the federal funds rate below 1% signals an emergency monetary easing in response to financial stress, which boosts risk appetite and liquidity, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS drops by > 0.75 percentage points in one month to below 1%
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are negative in more than 70% of triggered episodes, or the effect is absent outside of crisis periods.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both real personal savings (RSAFS) and personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) signals improved household balance sheets and stronger consumption confidence, which supports corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS and GDPC1 both show positive 3-month changes
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not statistically different from zero in triggered episodes, or the effect is reversed during periods of high inflation.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the unemployment rate above 6.5% for two consecutive months, regardless of other conditions, signals deteriorating labor market health and reduced consumer spending power, which leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the effect is not robust during periods of strong productivity growth.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous acceleration in industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) of more than 1% month-over-month indicates a broad-based supply-side expansion, which boosts corporate revenues and profit margins, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > 1% AND HOUST > 1% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive in triggered episodes, or the effect reverses during periods of high input cost inflation.
